This was a really well written article, and sums up my feelings for The Witcher 3 that I've been trying to put into words for weeks now. This last paragraph is exactly what I mean:

"With a blueprint for a successful open world on the table we can hope moving into the future that developers take note of the potential open worlds present beyond monotonous fetch quests and repetitive side missions. CDProject Red have shown with the right attitude and talent that an interactive world full of unique narratively driven side quests is genuinely achievable."
They did an incredible job making even the Witcher contracts, something that most game would have done pretty vanilla, unique and interesting. Like the article mentions you never know what to expect.

I'm a completionist when it comes to side quests too, and I've barely gotten into the main story despite putting in over 20 hours so far. I've been taking a break from it, but I need to get back in. :)

I got stuck on the contract where you have to find the wyrven nest - I climbed all the way up there expecting a tough boss fight (I was slightly underlevelled) only to be surprised that the monster I was searching for had a lady friend-monster who was equally pissed and deadly.

My Quen spamming was useless. RIP Geralt.

If it is the mission that I think it is there is a third one waiting for you after too. I did finish all of the contacts, the only things I hadn't finished are the gwent quests, the last fight club, and the horse races. I also need to replay near the end of the game since I apparently made the wrong choices and got the bad ending.

This game is ridiculously big. Not in a Dragon Age: Inquisition way where it's huge for the sake of having to trek across. I've spent over 100 hours and still haven't left Velen. There are still far more ? marks than things I have explored. Every side quest starts out simple enough and ends so differently than I could have imagined. The list just goes on and on. What a great game. I'll head to Skellige soon enough, and I hear it's even better.

My jaw-drop moment was when I realized I wasn't at the end game. The narrative was so well paced that I was convinced that would be the final scene. When I completed that and the following quest, the game said "right, off to Novigrad for you, you have stuff to do" and I was floored.

Working full time sucks because I can only put in a couple hours a night, but there's really nothing I'd rather be playing.
"Dad-time" when playing video games makes The Witcher 3 unbearable! I still love it, but when my free time amounts to about 90 minutes/night if I'm lucky, I feel like I'll never finish the damn game!

Right? It's just the gift that keeps on giving. Throw in those monster expansions they have coming as well as the consistent free DLC, and I might not play another game this year!
